Calyx · recorded research · no live account changes

Can Prop Ready fit a $1,000 account?

Five risk presets, the same nine strategies, and a separate extra-cost check. This is a shared-ledger replay of native standalone signals—not a native simultaneous portfolio backtest or a promise of live returns.

UTC window: 2026-08-17T00:00:00+00:00 → 2026-10-17T00:00:00+00:00 (end exclusive)
Starting cash: $1,000.00 · Target account specifications: Exness Technologies Ltd · Exness-MT5Trial15 · USD · 1:2000

Important: this is not an exact current-demo cost backtest. The connected target is Exness-MT5Trial15 (Pro-like contracts); fresh standalone sources use isolated Exness-MT5Trial16 (Raw-like pricing). Source US100 and USDJPY entry receipts include zero bid–ask spread plus recorded commissions, while the target demo snapshot spreads are positive. The base view retains source-account costs. The stress view adds a current-demo snapshot spread at each side plus doubled negative swap; this is a sensitivity, not exact replacement of Raw pricing with Pro pricing. Prices and fills can also differ. Neither view is a verified native backtest on your currently connected account.

No strategies, BATs, risk inputs or live positions were changed. Both existing DI filters remain ON; all five included ORBs retain 0.5R. The comparison changes only replay sizing and the explicit cost sensitivity.

What this window actually says
  • At fixed $5, 2 of 9 EAs admitted an order; 79 of 93 observed source entries were skipped for minimum lot size. The admitted subset closed 14 positions, returned -0.46%, and had PF 0.75. That is not execution of the full nine-EA profile.
  • The fixed-$2.50 view shows +0.31% and PF 45.57, but only 3 closed positions and $0.07 total recorded losses. A tiny denominator can inflate PF dramatically; it is not evidence of a dependable live edge or a recommended winner.
  • Do not raise risk just to force all strategies into a $1,000 account. First validate minimum-size compatibility and actual demo execution; changing contract sizes, capital or the reference cap requires separate testing.

Risk comparison · all presets

Percentage budgets use current sampled equity, but every preset still has the existing initial-reference cap of $5 per position. A 1% input therefore does not risk $10 here. The original source strategy’s lot request can impose a second ceiling. Minimum-size orders are skipped rather than rounded above the replay budget.

Min-lot stop risk comes from observed source entries and the target demo’s minimum lot. Reference-balance values are min / median / max of that risk ÷ 0.5%; they test only the reference-cap constraint, not margin or portfolio safety. A fixed-$5 allocation remains a $5 ceiling even at a larger balance. No source signals means no inferred capital requirement. An EA skipped for minimum size is operationally incompatible with this budget; a zero admitted return does not mean its strategy has no edge.

What the existing guards mean on $1,000

Per-position ceiling: $5 initial-stop risk, or the lower requested allocation/source lot ceiling. Stops and fills can slip.

Open risk: $22.50 overall; $15 on one symbol. This is not the same as a guaranteed daily maximum loss.

Daily reserved loss: $30 reference budget, including a 25% stop-risk reserve and $0.50 cash reserve per position.

Equity protection: $920 projected buffer; $900 hard reference floor; $50 hard day-anchor loss latch.

Frequency: at most seven entries and three net losing positions per Prague day; fixed priority and a three-second entry wait.

Compounding: percentage allocation changes with sampled equity; the original reference does not automatically rebase. Gains do not raise the $5 ceiling.

Guard thresholds are controls, not guaranteed realized loss caps. Gaps, slippage, simultaneous exposure, sample timing and broker execution can exceed an intended limit. A $1,000 account is not made safe by selecting high leverage, and this study does not support a reliable 2%-per-day or 10%-per-month target.

Practical next steps · not a live optimum

  • Solve order-size feasibility first. Keep the existing safety guards and skip orders whose true minimum-lot stop risk is too large. Do not tighten a strategy’s stop solely to make the lot size fit.
  • Use the demo to verify the actual order stream. Check broker costs, symbols, minimum lots, source-state differences and every skipped order before treating this research replay as attainable execution.
  • Do not call the 1% input full compounding. All five presets remain capped at $5 initial-stop risk here. Raising the reference cap or rebasing it after profits would be a new, separately tested risk policy—not something this replay authorizes.
  • Test smaller contract sizes or more capital separately. The minimum-capital estimates above only address one order’s stop-risk constraint; the same nine EAs still need simultaneous-risk and margin headroom.
  • Validate longer, unchanged rules before increasing risk. These two recent months cannot establish a best live percentage, dependable monthly income, or a low blow-up probability. A positive winner chosen here still needs forward demo evidence.

These are the current target-account contract, quote and read-only margin snapshots—not a historical spread or high-margin-requirement schedule. The replay prefers native entry-time source-account OrderCalcMargin receipts when recorded. Otherwise current buy/sell one-lot margins are scaled by historical entry price, except USD-base USDJPY where the fallback per-lot proxy is held fixed. Neither is certification of historical target Trial15 account margin tiers. Gross margin is reserved without hedging discounts.

Source-account recorded-cost view: Trial16 native source fills, spreads, commissions/fees and swaps are scaled to admitted lots, with entry and exit cash rounded to cents. This retains Raw-like source commissions and is not a current-demo Pro cost model. Native tester costs are not a certification of historical financing or real live execution.

Extra-cost sensitivity: one additional observed snapshot spread from the target Trial15 demo is charged at each side, and negative final swap is doubled. This is deliberately an extra charge on top of source fills and commissions, not replacement of the embedded spread or exact Pro repricing. Signals and exits are unchanged.

Initial risk prefers native entry-time source-account OrderCalcProfit receipts for the actual fill and original stop; filled-price geometry is only a fallback. Applying target minimum lots does not turn source-account receipts into exact historical Trial15 execution. The pre-request quote and slippage boundary are not reconstructible. MQL5 profit estimation and MQL5 margin estimation describe the broker/account-dependent calculations. Investor.gov: general leverage risks (not this CFD broker’s contract rules).

  • Two exposed months do not establish a durable edge or an optimal live risk setting.
  • Only observed standalone source fills are available; rejected trades can create unobserved later signals.
  • Sampled equity is not tick maximum drawdown; guard slippage, request budgets, cooldown wallclock and full current-SL timeline are not reconstructed.
  • Recorded costs are native tester costs, not verified historical commission/financing schedules.
  • Snapshot spreads and margins are sensitivities/estimates, not historic realized execution or fixed future conditions.
  • Risk presets were specified before replay results; choosing a live preset from just these two exposed months would still be retrospective selection.
  • Sharpe uses daily closed-cash returns on all 61 UTC calendar dates, including no-trade dates, annualized by √365 when supplied—not a confidence score. Daily cash tables use Prague dates for consistency with guard resets. PF and win streaks can be dominated by very few trades.
  • Minimum-lot skips mean a lower-risk preset may be a materially different admitted subset of the nine-strategy profile.
  • Daily sampled-equity protection, original-stop reservations and a margin proxy cannot reproduce every native guard state, current-stop modification, cooldown or simultaneous execution outcome.
